primitives.name: Blended Average Revenue Per User
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Blended ARPU ≈ Pro/Elite mix at founding monthly ≈ **~$18/mo** (mix-weighted).
primitives.assumptions: Fixed pricing tiers, fixed user mix, no promotional discounts.
primitives.breakdown_regime: At 0% conversion rate, ARPU becomes undefined; at 100% churn, ARPU decays to zero.

layer2.mapping: ARPU serves as input to MRR forecasting in GSE's stochastic state machine.
layer2.telemetry: Monthly recurring revenue (MRR) derived from active paying users.

primitives.name: Free-to-Paid Conversion Rate
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Assumptions (edit these — they drive everything) - Free→paid conversion: 2% (base), 1% (low), 4% (high).
primitives.assumptions: Conversion is independent of marketing spend or product quality in baseline.
primitives.breakdown_regime: At 0%, no revenue generated; at 100%, all free users become paid.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's user funnel transition probability matrix.
layer2.telemetry: Percentage of free users who convert within a given period.

primitives.name: Churn Elasticity
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Read of the model - The lever that matters most is **retention**, not acquisition — at 8%→5% churn the same funnel roughly doubles steady-state payers.
primitives.assumptions: Steady-state user base depends inversely on churn rate.
primitives.breakdown_regime: As churn approaches 100%, steady-state payers approach zero.

layer2.mapping: Used in GSE's retention optimization engine to compute long-term sustainability.

reasoning_traces.think:
The forecast scenario framework encodes a dual duality: pricing and conversion define the initial revenue potential, while retention and churn govern long-term sustainability. The blended ARPU acts as a kernel estimator for MRR under varying conversion and churn regimes. The free-to-paid conversion rate is a key driver of initial capital inflow, whereas churn elasticity determines the steady-state user base. These primitives form a closed-loop system where changes in one variable propagate through others, creating a feedback mechanism. For example, increasing conversion without improving retention leads to short-lived revenue spikes. Conversely, lowering churn without boosting conversion yields minimal growth. The model assumes independence among variables, which may fail under promotional campaigns or market saturation. The annual mix lever introduces temporal dimensionality by weighting upfront payments against recurring revenue streams. This structure enables GSE to simulate multiple user lifecycle paths and optimize for both immediate and long-term outcomes.
